title: Finding Pairs With a Certain Sum
statement:
Design a class `FindSumPairs` that holds two integer arrays, `nums1` and `nums2`, and answers questions about pairs made of one element from each. Only `nums2` ever changes.

- `FindSumPairs(nums1, nums2)` keeps the two arrays.
- `add(index, val)` raises `nums2[index]` by the positive amount `val`.
- `count(tot)` returns the number of index pairs `(i, j)`, where `i` ranges over the indices of `nums1` and `j` over those of `nums2`, for which `nums1[i] + nums2[j]` equals `tot` with the current values.
constraints: At most 1000 calls are made to add, and at most 1000 to count
notes:
## Intuition

Answering `count` by trying every pair costs `nums1.length × nums2.length` per query, which is far too slow when `nums2` is long. The two arrays have very different sizes: `nums1` is short and never changes, `nums2` is long and changes one cell at a time. So walk the short array and, for each `value` in it, ask how many cells of `nums2` hold `tot - value`. A frequency map over `nums2` answers that in O(1), and `add` only has to move one count from the old value to the new one.

## Approach

1. In the constructor, keep `nums1`, copy `nums2`, and build `freq`, mapping each value of `nums2` to how many times it appears.
2. `add(index, val)`: read the `old` value, compute `updated = old + val`, take one from `freq[old]`, add one to `freq[updated]`, and store `updated` in `nums2[index]`.
3. `count(tot)`: for each `value` of `nums1`, add `freq[tot - value]` (0 if missing) to `pairs`, then return `pairs`.

## Example 1, step by step

`nums2 = [1, 4, 5, 2, 5, 4]` gives `freq = {1: 1, 4: 2, 5: 2, 2: 1}`. `count(7)` walks `nums1 = [1, 1, 2, 2, 2, 3]`: each `1` needs a 6 (none), each of the three `2`s needs a 5 (2 each, 6 total) and `3` needs a 4 (2), so it returns `8`. `add(3, 2)` turns the `2` into a `4`: `freq[2] = 0`, `freq[4] = 3`. `count(8)` finds only `3 + 5` twice, so `2`; `count(4)` finds only `3 + 1`, so `1`. After `add(0, 1)` and `add(1, 1)` the map is `{2: 1, 4: 2, 5: 3}`, and `count(7)` gives `3 × 3` for the `2`s plus `2` for the `3`, which is `11`.

## Complexity

- Time: O(m) to build the map, O(1) per `add`, O(n) per `count`, where n = `nums1.length` and m = `nums2.length`.
- Space: O(m) for the copy of `nums2` and the map.

## Pitfalls

- Build the map over `nums2`, the long array, and loop over `nums1`; the other way round makes `count` cost O(m).
- `add` must update `nums2[index]` too, or the next `add` on that index removes the wrong value from the map.
- A missing key gives `undefined`; turn it into 0 before adding it to `pairs`.

## Variables

| Name | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `nums1` | the short, fixed array walked by `count` |
| `nums2` | the current values of the long array |
| `freq` | value of `nums2` → how many cells hold it |
| `old`, `updated` | the cell's value before and after `add` |
| `pairs` | running number of matching pairs in `count` |
| `value` | the current element of `nums1` |

narration.3: Keep the short array as it is; count will walk it.
narration.4: Copy the long array so later changes do not touch the caller's data.
narration.6: Count how often each value appears in nums2.
narration.7: One more cell holds this value.
narration.12: Read the value the cell holds before the change.
narration.13: Work out the value it will hold afterwards.
narration.14: That cell no longer holds the old value, so its count drops by one.
narration.15: It now holds the new value, so that count rises by one.
narration.16: Store the new value so a later add on this cell starts from it.
narration.21: Try every element of the short array as the left half of a pair.
narration.22: The right half must equal tot - value; the map says how many cells hold it.
narration.24: The sum over nums1 is the number of matching pairs.
